solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: After editing used to bin a little from speech

indicators.note: editing reworks and rearranges text, so once it is done these letters stand in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A speechwriter's draft is trimmed, with lines that were once in it binned during editing.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words used to bin rearrange into SOUNDBITE; the definition is the surface's own subject, a short extract from a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A soundbite is a short quotable extract taken from a longer speech or interview, broadcast on its own.

clue.text: Pressure to open secure lock in part of plant

indicators.note: a thing that opens something gets in between its sides, splitting the other word

parts.note: a seal is a fastening that keeps something securely closed
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone forces a stubborn lock on a greenhouse or plant room open.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes into SEAL after its first two letters to give SEPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepals are the small leaf-like parts of a flower that enclose and protect the bud before it opens.

clue.text: Howl grievously, worried after opera is given up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Lulu is Alban Berg's opera
ate in the sense of 'what's eating you?', meaning worried or troubled

explanation.surface: A disappointed fan wails miserably after an opera production is abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Lulu is Alban Berg's unfinished opera. 'Worried' as a past tense of eat uses the sense of a worry eating at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To ululate is to wail or howl loudly, traditionally as a lament for the dead or in grief.

clue.text: Making appearance, strangely enamoured

indicators.note: doing something strangely means not in the usual way, so these letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone smitten turns up acting oddly, appearing strangely in love.
explanation.walkthrough: ENAMOURED rearranges exactly into DEMEANOUR, the British spelling with -OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeanour is outward bearing or manner, the way a person looks and behaves to observers.

clue.text: Inside ourselves black bird is swallowed, not through the mouth

indicators.note: a thing gulped down ends up held within the body that gulped it

parts.note: into means to the inside of
the raven is a large all-black bird
us is the pronoun for ourselves

explanation.surface: A bird seems to have got inside us without being eaten, a medical puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests swallowing through the throat, but the definition rules the mouth out altogether: this is a drip or injection.
explanation.definitionFit: Intravenous drugs or fluids are delivered straight into a vein by drip or injection, bypassing oral intake.

clue.text: One not long hatched possibly walked off away from lake

indicators.note: being away from something means it is no longer present, so it is dropped

parts.note: to walk off is to leave, past tense left
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A newly hatched chick wanders off from the lakeside.
explanation.walkthrough: LEFT without L leaves EFT. 'Possibly' flags that a newt hatchling is only one kind of thing recently hatched.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a young newt, emerging from an egg, so it is a creature recently out of the egg.

clue.text: American natives start to clap opening of drama

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of clap
Act I is the first part of a play

explanation.surface: A theatre audience of Native Americans applauds as the play begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American natives' looks like people, but it means plants native to the Americas, where nearly all cacti originate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti are succulent plants that grow wild almost exclusively in North and South America, making them native there.

clue.text: See drivers picked up woman

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting letters up means reading them from the bottom

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation for drivers

explanation.surface: Watch some motorists offer a lift to a woman at the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: LO and RAC together read upwards give CAROL. 'Picked up' suggests a sound-alike, but here it turns the letters over.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol is a common female given name, so it stands for an example of a woman.

clue.text: Partner not a left-wing type?

parts.note: a Conservative, a Con, is not on the political left
a sort is a type or kind

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether their partner might be politically to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: Con is short for a member of Britain's Conservative Party, a right-wing type; the question mark flags the indirect clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a spouse or companion, especially the husband or wife of a reigning monarch.

clue.text: Fighting Puritans using clubs, dies in agony

parts.note: irons are golf clubs

indicators.note: someone in agony writhes and twists about, so these letters are contorted

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Puritan soldiers beat enemies with cudgels, and the victims perish in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' suggests cudgels in a battle scene, but these are golf clubs. Ironsides was the nickname of Cromwell's cavalry in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironsides was the name given to Oliver Cromwell's Puritan troopers, the soldiers of the Parliamentary army.

clue.text: In deep fall, fruit was satisfying

parts.note: a plum is a stone fruit
to meet a need is to satisfy it

explanation.surface: Late in autumn, the fruit harvest proved satisfying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' reads as autumn, the American season, but it is a drop. 'Was satisfying' is MET as in a demand met.
explanation.definitionFit: A plummet is a steep, sudden drop, as when prices or a falling object go sharply downward.

clue.text: Wrong to keep ahead at roundabout in city

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
on as in going on, forward or ahead
the letter O is round like a roundabout

explanation.surface: A driver goes the wrong way to stay in front at a traffic circle downtown.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is a legal wrong such as negligence; a roundabout is a British traffic circle, round like the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada and the capital of the province of Ontario.

clue.text: City wall has almost shrunk

indicators.note: something shrunk is smaller, its outer edges lost, so only a short run from the middle survives

parts.note: a run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A city wall has nearly collapsed and contracted.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'waLL HAS Almost'. 'City wall' looks like a unit, but City is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital of Tibet, the historic city of the Potala Palace.

clue.text: Nothing but cries of pain about the Serious Fraud Office: like this?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: nothing but means all, as in 'all talk'
SFO is the abbreviation for the British Serious Fraud Office
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Fraud investigators hear only howls of complaint and ask if this is how it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Serious Fraud Office is a UK government body that investigates and prosecutes major fraud; the question mark flags the definition as loose.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces what comes next, in the manner now to be described, much like saying thus.

clue.text: Fear old fire may explode in dire emergency

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things everywhere, so these letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: People fear an ancient fire might blow up in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: Fear, old and fire rearrange into the phrase; the surface's danger matches the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting for dear life means desperately, as if survival depends on it, as when clinging on in a crisis.

clue.text: Bow, rank being reduced

indicators.note: something reduced is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a row or rank in a series of levels

explanation.surface: Someone bows as they are demoted in rank.
explanation.walkthrough: TIER loses its last letter. 'Bow' reads as bending at the waist, but it is the knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow is a knot with loops, and also a short neck tie, so both senses are a kind of fastening.

clue.text: Undistinguished types man such a ship?

parts.note: identical twins are hard to tell apart
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: Ordinary nobodies staff a vessel of a certain kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undistinguished' suggests unremarkable, but here it means not distinguishable from one another. The definition depends on reading the wordplay as a ship crewed by twins.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-screw ship has two propellers, one on each side, driven by separate shafts.

clue.text: Bursting from covert, a deer panicked unnecessarily?

indicators.note: something bursting flies apart, so these letters come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A frightened deer bolts from its thicket though nothing was threatening it.
explanation.walkthrough: A covert is a thicket where game hides. The question mark flags that the definition is also the deer's story.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreact is to respond more strongly than a situation warrants, such as panicking without cause.

clue.text: Make light of a patriarch delayed coming round

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: coming round something means encircling it, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: delayed means late
Levi, son of Jacob, is one of the Old Testament patriarchs

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off an elder of the family arriving late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make light of' suggests mocking or dismissing, but the definition is making a burden lighter, with 'of' only joining.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate is to lessen suffering or a burden, making it easier to bear.

clue.text: In pink clothes small opening with no body visible

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap around it, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: coral is a pinkish colour
a pore is a tiny opening in skin

explanation.surface: Someone dressed in pink has only a tiny gap showing, no flesh exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' reads as garments, but it is a verb meaning wraps around.
explanation.definitionFit: Incorporeal means lacking material form, like a spirit or ghost without any physical substance.

clue.text: Firm punishment announced for Charlie

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: what is announced is spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the cane was a school punishment; the spelling matches the surname Caine

explanation.surface: A strict penalty is declared for a man called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like a man's name, but it is slang for the drug, from its initial C.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie is British slang for cocaine, from the phonetic alphabet word for its first letter.

clue.text: Vehicle broken down, back falling off

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, and it falling off means the final letter goes

parts.note: bust means broken

explanation.surface: A broken-down vehicle shedding its rear panel.
explanation.walkthrough: BUST loses its last letter, the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a large road vehicle carrying passengers along a set route.

clue.text: Town providing duke's overnight accommodation?

parts.note: a bed is where one stays the night
providing for someone, as in supplied for
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A town that put up a visiting duke for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the clue is BED FOR D. There is also a real Duke of Bedford.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedford is the county town of Bedfordshire in England, a market town on the River Great Ouse.

clue.text: Triumph for female going next in line

parts.note: a triumph is a success

indicators.note: something going is leaving, so it is dropped from the word beside it

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman wins out by being next in line for the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: SUCCESS then 'for' without F, leaving OR. 'For female' looks like a phrase, but female is removed from for.
explanation.definitionFit: A successor is the person who follows another in an office or title, next to inherit it.

clue.text: Turn out European winner, having no alternative

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: having no part of something means it is left out

parts.note: a victor is a winner
or is the word that offers an alternative

explanation.surface: A European champion turns up with no other option available.
explanation.walkthrough: E then VICTOR without OR. 'Turn out' looks like appearing, but it means throw out.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to expel a tenant from a property, putting them out of their home.

clue.text: Recording verb one dictionary rejected

parts.note: v is the dictionary abbreviation for verb
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so its letters run the other way

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A recording made for a dictionary entry has a verb the editors turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: V and I, then OED turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: A video is a recording of moving images, the thing itself or the act of making one.

clue.text: One has depressing experience, losing daughter

indicators.note: losing something means it is no longer there, so it comes out

parts.note: a downer is something depressing
d is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone goes through a sad time after their daughter leaves or dies.
explanation.walkthrough: DOWNER without its D. 'One has' reads as the start of a sentence, but it defines one who has, a possessor.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is a person who possesses something, so one who has it is an owner.

clue.text: Barrier's resistance weakening

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance
ailing means getting weaker or sick

explanation.surface: A barricade is starting to give way.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', joining the definition to R plus AILING.
explanation.definitionFit: A railing is a fence or barrier made of rails, such as along a balcony or staircase.

clue.text: Pain as Arab country has borders reduced

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, so cutting them removes the outermost letters

parts.note: Egypt is an Arab country

explanation.surface: Losing territory along its frontiers hurts a Middle Eastern nation.
explanation.walkthrough: EGYPT loses its first and last letters. Gyp is British informal for pain, as in 'my back is giving me gyp'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyp is British slang for pain or discomfort, usually in the phrase giving someone gyp.

clue.text: I had turned over a New Statesman

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turning a word around makes it run the other way

parts.note: taken as written
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to changing sides about the political magazine the New Statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned over' looks like one phrase, but turned acts on had and over is O. The New Statesman is a British political weekly.
explanation.definitionFit: Read cryptically, a statesman is a man from a US state, and an Idahoan is a native of Idaho.

clue.text: Forcibly seize snooker equipment from reporter

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the news, so the word comes as it is spoken

parts.note: a rest is the cross-headed stick that supports a snooker cue for a long shot

explanation.surface: A journalist grabs the cue rest at a snooker match.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest is snooker's cue-support stick; the definition is a verb, to wrench something away.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest is to pull something away by force, wrenching it from someone's grip.

clue.text: Not yet properly cooked, one claims?

parts.note: pre- means before, not yet
meat cooked properly becomes tender

explanation.surface: A cook insists the dish is not ready yet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: 'one claims' means a person who lays a claim, as to a throne.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender is a claimant to a title or throne, such as the Old and Young Pretenders of Stuart history.
